text:
maria: quick sync — customer-alpha generated a burst of audit events for ~2h, our audit-ingest consumer lagged out and cost popped. KMS per-event calls are the biggest culprit i think. anyone else seeing this?
julian: saw the alerts. shard 7 lagged ~45m, reprocessed 120M events. cost calc shows KMS RPCs added ~0.08 USD/event at peak (so ugly).
anika: ouch. were those events signed/encrypted with customer KMS or our envelope key?
maria: envelope key via KMS Encrypt per event — yes. customer had RBAC change that created a flood of "role:update" events.
kai: can we batch encrypt or switch to envelope-with-local-cache? per-event KMS is expensive and adds latency.
anika: we already have an envelope key design but the implementation does one KMS call on write. we could change to periodic rewrap + local ephemeral data-key cache to avoid per-event calls. risky but doable.
julian: short-term mitigation: sample or drop noisy event types for high-volume tenants and mark as "audit.sampled" until we fix. long-term: key caching + group signing.
maria: need to validate customer-facing audit schema first — some customers expect full fields for role.audit events. if we sample we must ensure compliance customers still get full fidelity.
jen_ops: +1. can we toggle per-tenant retention/verbosity flags? maybe a quick feature flag for enterprise tenants to keep full fidelity while sampling others.
kai: config snippet for consumer batching I tested in staging: ```consumer.batch.max_bytes=5mb
consumer.batch.max_events=200
consumer.flush.interval_ms=250```
reduced KMS pressure by ~4x in my run.
julian: nice. also increased elasticsearch refresh interval for audit-index to 30s during surge to reduce indexing cost. did that show improvement?
kai: yes ~30% decrease in indexing ops — but search latency briefly increased. tradeoff acceptable for ingest heavy windows.
anika: schema validation question: we found a few older services emitting legacy fields that cause our validator to reject batched events. should we run a compatibility pass that auto-maps legacy fields to v2?
maria: prefer explicit mapping with warning logs rather than silent auto-fix. we must keep an audit trail of transformations for customers.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: audit-ingest-batching-v2 -> staging at 12:05 UTC.
julian: action items: 1) enable per-tenant sampling FF (maria) 2) implement data-key cache prototype (kai) 3) compatibility mapping + warning (anika) 4) cost model calc for KMS vs rewrap vs local (jen_ops). can we get rough ETA?
maria: I'll own the FF, can do rollout in <24h.
kai: prototype for key cache by EOD tomorrow.
anika: compatibility mapping PR by end of week, tests included.
jen_ops: I'll run cost model with historical traffic; will share numbers in this thread.
maria: one more thing — RBAC change that triggered this came from a bulk API that we should throttle on master. adding a short-term rate-limit on role-change endpoints could prevent repeat.
julian: agree. add route-level throttle + circuit-breaker. low-risk and immediate.
maria: thanks all. i'll open a quick runbook section for "audit-volume surge" with mitigation steps (samplingFF, throttle, temp index relax). posting draft in #incidents later. :thumbsup:
jen_ops: adding cost snapshot to the draft now. will tag the affected customers for follow-up.
kai: testing shows local key-cache + batching reduces KMS ops by ~92% in our sim. big win.
anika: once we have mapping and cache, we should run a canary on a non-compliance test tenant to double-check no required events are lost.
maria: agreed. schedule canary after deploy-bot completes. thanks everyone!
